passage: I'm Pranati, and for two years the certification exam lived in a folder called someday. Last September I made a plan: twelve weeks, one module a week. Then I asked Kamal, a colleague in the finance team, if we could meet every Friday at four for ten minutes. I would show what I had finished, and Kamal would only ask, "Is that what you planned?" No advice, no praise. The first Friday I had not finished the module and my face went hot. The second Friday I had. By week eight I noticed I was starting on Monday mornings just so my page would not look empty on Friday. I passed on the first try. I still keep Fridays with Kamal for other things.

qa.a: They met every Friday at four for ten minutes.

qa.a: Kamal might feel useful and glad that one simple question was enough to help.

Team manager's note, quarterly review: Sangeeta

In March, Sangeeta told me she wanted to finish a cloud certification by June, alongside her normal work. She made a plan with six milestones. What I noticed was the next step. She asked Zeenat, a colleague who had passed the same exam last year, to meet her every Friday at five for fifteen minutes. Each Friday Sangeeta showed what she had done that week: notes, a practice test score, a lab screenshot. Twice she had nothing to show, and Zeenat simply asked, "What got in the way, and what's the plan for next week?" I saw Sangeeta rearrange her evenings after that. She passed the exam on June 18. I've suggested she share this method with the new joiners.

qa.q: When did Sangeeta pass the exam?
How might Sangeeta have felt on the Fridays she had nothing to show?
qa.a: She probably felt embarrassed and a bit guilty, which pushed her to rearrange her evenings.

qa.q: How could the new joiners use this method?
qa.a: Each could pick a colleague who has done the course, set a short weekly meeting and show real work each time.

qa.q: How might Zeenat see her part in this?
qa.a: Zeenat likely felt useful and proud, since fifteen minutes a week helped a colleague pass.

grounding: A young professional meets a colleague every Friday to show progress on a certification, which helps her keep to the schedule.

Friday

Fourth Friday with Disha today. I showed her my practice test, 71 out of 100, up from 58 last week. She circled the networking questions and said, "That's your weak spot." It felt good to have someone look at it. I know I would have skipped this week without her. On Wednesday I was so tired I nearly didn't open the book, but then I thought of sitting in front of Disha at five on Friday with nothing to show, and I did one chapter. It's a strange kind of help. She doesn't push, she just asks. And somehow that's enough. Next milestone: networking chapter plus one full mock test before next Friday. Himani, you've got this.
